title: Exactness of actual scalar localization on module sheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $s\in\Gamma(\mathcal C,R)$ be a global section. Use the abelian categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Put $R_s=R[1/s]$, the sheafification of $V\mapsto R(V)[1/s|_V]$, with its canonical ring map $\varphi:R\to R_s$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. Let $E:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_s)$ be actual change of rings $E(M)=R_s\otimes_R M$, using sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $E(f)=1\otimes f$ on morphisms. Then $E$ is additive and exact: it preserves finite limits and finite colimits, or equivalently sends every short exact sequence of $R$-module sheaves to a short exact sequence of $R_s$-module sheaves. The same assertion holds for any functor equipped with a natural isomorphism to this actual change-of-rings functor. No point, enough-points, scheme, nonzero, or boundedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03ET (lemma-flatness-sheafification), applied to the presheaf of section localizations; exactness as a scalar-extension functor extracted from that flatness assertion.

proof.text: Let $P$ be the presheaf of $R$-algebras $P(V)=R(V)[1/s|_V]$, with the localization restriction maps of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. For every $V$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat] to the multiplicative subset $\{1,s|_V,(s|_V)^2,\ldots\}$ of the commutative ring $R(V)$. Thus $P(V)$ is flat over $R(V)$. This argument also permits $0$ in the multiplicative subset: if $s|_V$ is nilpotent then $P(V)=0$, which is flat.
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sectionwise-flat-presheaf-tensor] to $P$ from step 1. It gives precisely the finite-limit hypothesis on $-\otimes_{p,R}P$, including kernels and the empty product.

source.place: Tag 03ES (lemma-flatness-presheaves), with the finite-limit formulation of presheaf flatness in Tag 03ER (definition-flat), (1); explicit kernel and finite-product comparisons extracted from the sectionwise proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-sheafification-flat] with $\mathcal O=R$ and $\mathcal F=P$, using step 2. As $R$ is already a sheaf, $R^\#=R$, and by construction $P^\#=R_s$ as an $R$-module. Thus $R_s$ is a flat $R$-module sheaf. By [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], $M\mapsto M\otimes_R R_s$ is exact as an endofunctor of $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. The symmetry and additivity in [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] give that $T(M)=R_s\otimes_R M$, with $T(f)=1\otimes f$, is an additive exact endofunctor of $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$.

Put $V=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]; it keeps the underlying abelian sheaf, so $U_{R_s}=U_RV$ for the forgetful functors of step 5. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-tensor-comparison], $VE(M)\cong T(M)$ by the identity on local pure tensors. This is natural in $M$: both arrow maps send $b\otimes m$ to $b\otimes f(m)$, so agree before sheafification and hence after it. Thus $VE\cong T$.

source.place: Section 03CV (section-sheaves-modules), change-of-rings paragraphs and lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; Section 03EK (tensor product); Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules).

proof.text: For $A=R,R_s$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] gives faithful exact $U_A:\operatorname{Mod}(A)\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$, with the same underlying kernels and cokernels. Exactness is detected there: an underlying zero sheaf has only zero sections, hence is the zero module sheaf. Since $U_{R_s}E\cong U_RT$, $E$ preserves short exact sequences. Faithfulness and preservation of sums by $U_{R_s}$ and $T$ give $E(f+g)=E(f)+E(g)$ and $E(0)=0$.

In the abelian module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], factor an arrow $a:M\to N$ into the short exact sequences $0\to\ker a\to M\to\operatorname{im}a\to0$ and $0\to\operatorname{im}a\to N\to\operatorname{coker}a\to0$. Step 5 identifies $E(\ker a)$ and $E(\operatorname{coker}a)$ as its kernel and cokernel. Additivity preserves the finite biproduct equations, including zero. Finite limits and colimits are kernels and cokernels of the differences of incidence maps between those biproducts; hence $E$ preserves both. If $\alpha:F\cong E$, then $F(f)=\alpha_N^{-1}E(f)\alpha_M$, giving additivity; its components identify the image short exact sequences, giving exactness and the same finite preservation.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian); paragraph following Tag 03DB, referring to homology-lemma-exact-functor; elementary biproduct/kernel formulas and natural-isomorphism conjugation.
